subject: Request: site-specific DPF evidence + datastore flow maps
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthbridgecorp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@healthbridgecorp.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: HealthBridge: site-specific DPF evidence and datastore mapping request

Hi Tessa / Monica,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of our procurement/compliance checklist we need site-specific evidence to validate cross-border transfer safeguards under the EU Data Protection Framework. Attached is a short workbook with the items we need for each Redwood processing location that may touch EU personal data. Primary asks are:

- Confirmation of lawful basis and role for processing (controller vs processor) for each product surface (API/embeddings/logs).
- Transfer mechanism used for EU->US processing (DPF binding, SCCs, adequacy, or other) and any relevant effective dates.
- High-level datastore flow map for EU-hosted traffic (S3 buckets, replication, backups) and any transient caching outside EU.
- Sub-processor list impacting EU data, with country locations and whether subprocessors have separate DPF coverage.
- Technical measures: encryption at rest/in transit, KMS usage (customer-managed vs Redwood), pseudonymization/anonymization options, and retention windows for logs and KV caches.

Can you provide an initial package by EOD (UTC) today or confirm a delivery time? Ideally we need a diagram per site, a one-page assurance summary, and any redacted example logs if helpful.

Appreciate it — we’ll expedite contractual path once we have these artifacts.

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement 
HealthBridge Corp

Attachments: HealthBridge_DPF_Request_v1.xlsx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:24:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: HealthBridge: site-specific DPF evidence and datastore mapping request

Folks — forwarding HealthBridge’s workbook. They specifically asked for site-level diagrams and explicit transfer mechanism statements (DPF vs SCCs). Can Neha and Rachel put together the technical evidence and a redacted EU S3/dataflow diagram? Monica, can you confirm whether we should assert DPF coverage or SCCs for this customer (region: EU)?

Proposed split:
- Neha: technical measures, KMS details, retention and pseudonymization write-up + attach dpf-evidence-summary.pdf.
- Rachel: create per-site flow diagram (redwood-eu-s3-dataflow.png) and list of subprocessors with country mapping.
- Monica: legal/controls note — confirm transfer mechanism and provide DPA annex extract (dpa-annex-extract.txt).

Timeline: HealthBridge asked for EOD UTC. If we can’t hit that, let’s commit to a 24-hour window and tell them.

Thanks — Tessa

Subject: Re: Fwd: HealthBridge: site-specific DPF evidence and datastore mapping request

Tessa — attaching a first-pass bundle. Key points below (I included short-form language we can send to HealthBridge):

1) Role and lawful basis
- Redwood Inference acts as a processor for customer-provided prompts and embeddings. Customers typically remain the controller for user data they submit. We will sign the DPA and DPA Annex to reflect processor obligations.

2) Transfer mechanism
- For EU-origin data sent to Redwood-hosted endpoints in EU regions that require additional processing in the US, Redwood relies on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) for the Redwood corporate accounts that are DPF-certified. Where DPF does not apply (e.g., certain subprocessors or legacy connectors), we rely on the updated SCCs. We recommend asserting DPF as the primary mechanism and referencing SCC fallback in the DPA annex.

3) Technical measures (summary)
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ for all API traffic; mutual TLS for private deployments where configured.
- At rest: default AES-256 encryption for object stores and block storage.
- KMS: Redwood-managed KMS by default (customer-managed KMS supported for Dedicated/Private deployments).
- KV/cache: ephemeral KV caches are encrypted and TTL-limited; persistent request logs retained per customer-configured retention (default 30 days for logs, 90 days for metrics).
- Pseudonymization: we support per-customer tokenization/pseudonymization pipelines before non-EU egress; recommend can be configured as an ingestion step.

4) Subprocessors and locations
- Attached is the current subprocessor list with country mapping. EU-facing processing uses primary clusters in eu-west-1 / europe-west as applicable. Some analytics and model fine-tuning jobs may use US-hosted services which are covered under corporate DPF.

5) Artifacts attached (zipped in the bundle)
- dpf-evidence-summary.pdf (controls matrix + certification snapshot)
- redwood-eu-s3-dataflow.png (single-page flow diagram, redacted for public sharing)
- subprocessor-countries.csv
- sample redacted logs (redacted-logs-sample.txt)
- dpa-annex-extract.txt (legal excerpt for DPA annex)

I think we can send a combined package to HealthBridge. If Liam needs full unredacted diagrams or bucket names, we should request an LOA/NDA.

Neha

Attachments: dpf-evidence-summary.pdf; redwood-eu-s3-dataflow.png; subprocessor-countries.csv; redacted-logs-sample.txt; dpa-annex-extract.txt

Hi team — good work. A few edits before we send externally:

- Transfer mechanism language: state primary reliance on DPF for Redwood corporate accounts and processors that are DPF-certified, and include a short sentence noting SCCs are used as a contractual fallback where subprocessors are outside DPF scope. Avoid absolute statements about "always DPF".
- Retention: confirm we provide a customer-configured option and the default values (logs 30 days; metrics 90 days) and note we can extend on a contract.
- Diagrams: redwood-eu-s3-dataflow.png looks fine as a redacted version. Please remove specific bucket names and replace with placeholders (we have done that already).
- DPA annex: attach the extract and add a line that the full DPA Annex will be included in our contracting package; include hyperlink to canonical DPA page (internal link).

I can take final pass on wording for the legal paragraph. Once Neha and Rachel confirm the final artifacts, Tessa can send to Liam with the note that we can book a 30m technical walkthrough if they want deeper detail.

Monica

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Please find attached the initial evidence bundle and a short summary below. If you'd like a deeper walkthrough, we can schedule a 30-minute technical session this week.

What we attached (redacted for procurement):
- dpf-evidence-summary.pdf — certification snapshot and controls matrix (DPF certification ID redacted for procurement sharing).
- redwood-eu-s3-dataflow.png — per-site redacted dataflow showing EU ingress, ephemeral KV/cache behavior, and points of transient US egress for model analytics jobs.
- dpa-annex-extract.txt — excerpt of DPA Annex language and fallback to SCCs where DPF coverage does not apply.
- HealthBridge_DPF_Request_v1_filled.xlsx — our short-form answers inline in your workbook.

Short answers (high level):
- Role: Redwood acts as a processor for customer-provided content (prompts, files, embeddings) and processes per the DPA. Customers act as the controller for data they collect/submit.
- Transfer mechanism: Primary mechanism — EU-US Data Privacy Framework for Redwood corporate accounts and services covered by our certification. Where subprocessors or specific connectors fall outside DPF, we rely on updated SCCs as a contractual fallback.
- Technical controls: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest; Redwood-managed KMS by default (customer-managed KMS available on Dedicated/Private); KV caches are ephemeral, encrypted, and TTL-limited.
- Subprocessors: attached list with country mappings. Most EU-facing processing occurs in EU regions; select analytics/modeling jobs run in the US and are covered under our corporate DPF account or SCCs.
- Retention & logs: default retention windows are documented in the workbook; we support contract-level changes (logs default 30 days).

Next steps:
1) If you require unredacted diagrams (bucket names, exact cluster IDs), we will need an LOA/NDA and can provision a protected share.
2) If this package meets the ask, confirm and we'll attach the same language into the draft DPA Annex for signature.
3) Book a 30-minute tech deep-dive if desired — Monica and Neha can join.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpf-evidence-summary.pdf; redwood-eu-s3-dataflow.png; dpa-annex-extract.txt; HealthBridge_DPF_Request_v1_filled.xlsx
